newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-ANDREWS AND HULBERT WIN JCPENNEY CLASSIC.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-ANDREWS AND HULBERT WIN JCPENNEY CLASSIC.

text.p: The team of Donna Andrews and Mike Hulbert combined for a final-round 3-under-par 68 on Sunday to claim a one-stroke victory at the rain-shortened JCPenney Classic golf tournament.
Andrews and Hulbert, who shared the lead with Pat Hurst and Scott McCarron entering Sunday's round, finished at 16-under 197 at the Innisbrook Hilton Copperhead course.
The winners split $375,000 for their victory in the special event that pairs members of the PGA Tour with LPGA Tour players.
The tandem of reigning U.S. Amateur champions Kelli Kuehne and Tiger Woods tied for second with Missie McGeorge and Joel Edwards at 15-under 198.
Kuehne and PGA rookie sensation Woods carded a final 68, while McGeorge and Edwards combined for a 67. Hurst and McCarron finished another stroke back at 14-under 199 after carding a 70.

The tournament was reduced to 54 holes for the first time in its 37-year history due to heavy rain Saturday. The final round was played in the alternate shot format, the same format used Friday. A best-ball format was used in the first round.
Andrews and Hulbert combined for birdies on the first, fourth and sixth holes on the front nine and added another on 12. A bogey on the par-5 14th was their only blemish.
"My partner (Hulbert) was telling me how good I was putting and that gave me a lot of confidence," said Andrews, a four-time winner on the LPGA Tour.
"It's a team event and we kept that in mind," said Hulbert, who has won three PGA events in his 12-year career.
"My partner played so good this week and I played good at times. Donna rolled in putts all week."
Woods and Kuehne had an uneven final round. Kuehne admitted later she was not quite prepared for all the commotion surrounding her partner.
"Dealing with the people is a lot harder than it looks. With all the people following Tiger, it was a big shock," Kuehne said.
"Her first time out she was a little tight, a little nervous, and I was the same way," said Woods, who won two tournaments after turning professional late in the season.
First-round leaders Laura Davies and John Daly, the longest drivers on their respective tours, finished in a tie for fifth with Dottie Pepper and Jeff Sluman at 13-under 200.
The Swedish duo of Annika Sorenstam and Jesper Parnevik led a group of four teams at 12-under 201.
Defending champions, Beth Daniel and Davis Love, shot a final-round 68 to finish at 10-under.
